blocks.prompt: 2 (i) On the same axes and to the same scale, draw the graphs of the following functions for their complete period: \(y = \sin x\) and \(y = \sin 2x\).
blocks.explanation:
Yahan do sine curves ek hi graph par banane hain taa ke in ka muqabla ho sake: unchai ek jaisi, lekin raftaar alag.
Plan: \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\) ki ek table jis mein dono functions hon, dono plot karenge, aur dekhenge ke curves kahan milte hain.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \sin x\) aur \(y = \sin 2x\).
Humein banana hai: dono ke graphs ek hi axes par, complete period ke liye.
Tareeqa: \(\sin x\) ka period \(2\pi\) hai aur \(\sin 2x\) ka \(\pi\). Is liye \([0, 2\pi]\) par pehla function ek poora chakkar aur doosra do poore chakkar lagata hai; yahi dono ka complete period dikhane ke liye kaafi hai. 'same axes, same scale' ka matlab: ek hi graph par dono curves, aur dono ke liye x aur y ke khaane ek jaise, taa ke in ka muqabla (comparison) saaf nazar aaye.

Amplitudes aur periods
\[\sin x:\ \text{amplitude } 1,\ \text{period } 2\pi\]
\[\sin 2x:\ \text{amplitude } 1,\ \text{period } \pi\]
Kyun: andar wala 2 period aadha karta hai lekin unchai nahi badalta. Is liye dono curves \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan hi rahenge.

Table of values (jawab ke neeche di gayi hai)
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}:\ \sin x \approx 0.71,\ \sin 2x = 1\]
\[x = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}:\ \sin x \approx 0.71,\ \sin 2x = -1\]
Kyun: \(\pi/4\) \(\sin 2x\) ka quarter period hai, is liye is ke saare peaks aur zeros table mein aa jate hain. \(\sin 2x\) ke liye pehle angle \(2x\) banayein, phir sine lein.
Dhyan dein: \(\sin 2x\) ko \(2\sin x\) na samjhein; \(2\sin x\) ki unchai 2 hoti, jabke \(\sin 2x\) ki unchai 1 hi hai.

Dono curves plot karein
\(y = \sin x\): \(\pi/2\) par 1 tak upar, \(3\pi/2\) par \(-1\) tak neeche, ek chakkar. \(y = \sin 2x\): \(\pi/4\) aur \(5\pi/4\) par 1, \(3\pi/4\) aur \(7\pi/4\) par \(-1\), do chakkar.
Kyun: ek hi grid par dono ko dekh kar foran samajh aata hai ke \(\sin 2x\) do guna tez dohraya jata hai. Dono curves alag rang ya alag lakeer se banayein aur un par naam likhein.

Curves kahan milte hain
\[\sin 2x = \sin x\]
\[2\sin x\cos x - \sin x = 0\]
\[\sin x\,(2\cos x - 1) = 0\]
\[x = 0,\ \dfrac{\pi}{3},\ \pi,\ \dfrac{5\pi}{3},\ 2\pi\]
Kyun: \(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\) (double angle formula). \(\sin x\) common nikala. \(\sin x = 0\) se \(0, \pi, 2\pi\), aur \(\cos x = 1/2\) se \(\pi/3, 5\pi/3\). Yahi points graph par crossing ki soorat mein nazar aate hain.

Tasdeeq
\[\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} \approx 0.87\]
Kyun: \(x = \pi/3\) par dono curves ki unchai 0.87 hai, yani waqai wahan milte hain.
Yaad rakhein: \(\sin cx\) mein \(c\) jitna bara, lehar utni ghani (zyada chakkar); \(c\) chhota ho to lehar phaili hui. Is sawal ka asal sabaq yahi hai, aur graph par dono curves saath dekh kar yeh baat hamesha ke liye yaad ho jati hai.
blocks.final_answer: \([0, 2\pi]\) par: \(y = \sin x\) ek chakkar (period \(2\pi\)) aur \(y = \sin 2x\) do chakkar (period \(\pi\)) lagata hai, dono ka amplitude 1; curves \(x = 0, \pi/3, \pi, 5\pi/3, 2\pi\) par milte hain.

answer_figure.alt: y = sin x and y = sin 2x on the same axes from 0 to 2 pi: sin x makes one cycle, sin 2x makes two; they meet at x = 0, pi/3, pi, 5 pi/3 and 2 pi.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) On the same axes and to the same scale, draw the graphs of the following functions for their complete period: \(y = \cos x\) and \(y = \cos 2x\).
blocks.explanation:
Ab do cosine curves ek graph par: unchai ek jaisi, lekin \(\cos 2x\) do guna tez.
Plan: \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\) ki ek table, dono curves plot, aur milne ke points. Yeh bilkul part (i) jaisa hai, bas sine ki jagah cosine; is liye part (i) ka tareeqa yahan bhi qadam ba qadam chalega.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \cos x\) aur \(y = \cos 2x\).
Humein banana hai: dono ke graphs ek hi axes par, complete period ke liye.
Tareeqa: \(\cos x\) ka period \(2\pi\) aur \(\cos 2x\) ka \(\pi\). \([0, 2\pi]\) par pehla ek aur doosra do chakkar lagata hai. Ek table, ek hi axes, ek hi scale, taa ke dono ka muqabla seedha nazar aaye. Dono curves alag rang mein banayein aur naam likhein.

Amplitudes aur periods
\[\cos x:\ \text{amplitude } 1,\ \text{period } 2\pi\]
\[\cos 2x:\ \text{amplitude } 1,\ \text{period } \pi\]
Kyun: angle ke andar wala 2 sirf period badalta hai, unchai nahi.

Table of values
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}:\ \cos x = 0,\ \cos 2x = -1\]
\[x = \pi:\ \cos x = -1,\ \cos 2x = 1\]
Kyun: \(\pi/4\) ke qadam \(\cos 2x\) ke har peak aur zero ko pakar lete hain. \(\cos 2x\) ke liye pehle angle double karein: \(x = \pi/2\) par angle \(\pi\), aur \(\cos\pi = -1\).
Dhyan dein: \(\cos 2x\) ko \(2\cos x\) na samjhein; \(2\cos x\) ki unchai 2 hoti.

Dono curves plot karein
\(y = \cos x\): 0 par 1, \(\pi\) par \(-1\), \(2\pi\) par wapas 1. \(y = \cos 2x\): \(0, \pi, 2\pi\) par 1 aur \(\pi/2, 3\pi/2\) par \(-1\).
Kyun: har cosine curve apne maximum 1 se shuru hota hai, is liye dono curves \(x = 0\) par ek hi point se shuru hote hain.

Curves kahan milte hain
\[\cos 2x = \cos x\]
\[2\cos^2 x - \cos x - 1 = 0\]
\[(\cos x - 1)(2\cos x + 1) = 0\]
\[x = 0,\ \dfrac{2\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{4\pi}{3},\ 2\pi\]
Kyun: \(\cos 2x = 2\cos^2 x - 1\) rakh kar \(\cos x\) mein quadratic equation bani, jise factorize kiya. \(\cos x = 1\) se \(0, 2\pi\), aur \(\cos x = -1/2\) se \(2\pi/3, 4\pi/3\) (doosra aur teesra quadrant, jahan cosine negative hai).

Tasdeeq
\[\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = -\dfrac12,\ \cos\dfrac{4\pi}{3} = -\dfrac12\]
Kyun: \(x = 2\pi/3\) par \(\cos 2x = \cos(4\pi/3) = -1/2\) bhi. Dono curves ki unchai \(-0.5\), to milna sahi hai.
Yaad rakhein: graph par dono curves ke milne ke points hamesha algebra se check kar lein; agar graph aur algebra ek jaisa jawab dein to aap ka graph sahi scale par bana hai.
blocks.final_answer: \([0, 2\pi]\) par: \(y = \cos x\) ek chakkar (period \(2\pi\)) aur \(y = \cos 2x\) do chakkar (period \(\pi\)), dono ka amplitude 1; curves \(x = 0, 2\pi/3, 4\pi/3, 2\pi\) par milte hain.
